title: Burstwave session synthesizer and snapshot reporter for kernel drift analysis
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: We need a lightweight, reproducible session-level workload synthesizer that can generate short-lived burst patterns (temporal spikes) and multi-phase sessions to reproduce kernel scheduling and KV cache pressure seen in production p95/p99 tails. Motivation: Existing runners produce steady-state sequences or reproduce long tail distributions but do not emulate multi-phase sessions with rapid intra-session bursts followed by quiet periods. This gap blocks iteration on scheduling heuristics and per-kernel latency drift mitigation experiments.

This PR introduces two components in the benchmark-lab runner suite: 1) Burstwave Session Synthesizer: a configurable workload generator that composes sessions from phases (startup ramp, burstwave, cooldown, intermittent microbursts). It supports parameterized sequence lengths, token emission rate profiles, KV cache warm/cold toggles, and per-session seed control for deterministic replay. 2) Snapshot Reporter: a compact per-run reporter that samples per-kernel latency distributions at snapshot points (pre-burst, peak-burst, post-burst) and emits a small lineage metadata file that ties snapshots to run configuration and random seeds.

Why unique: Instead of only collecting global latency histograms, the reporter captures per-kernel (attention, softmax, GEMM, memcopy) percentiles at three logical snapshots and serializes them for differential analysis across commits. This makes small regressions in a single kernel visible without needing full flamegraphs, enabling faster CI feedback on kernel changes.

High-level changes: - tools/session_synthesizer/burstwave.py: new synthesizer with CLI and YAML profile support. - tools/reporters/snapshot_reporter.py: new reporter that hooks into runner lifecycle and emits compressed snapshots. - benchmark-lab/config/profiles/burstwave-default.yaml: canonical profile used in CI. - tests/integration/test_burstwave_replay.py: deterministic replay + golden snapshot assertions. - benchci/pipelines/burstwave.yaml: ephemeral CI job definition for nightly regression runs. - docs/bench-lab/burstwave-readme.md: usage and tuning guide.

Checklist: - [x] Synthesizer implementation and CLI. - [x] Snapshot serialization and lineage metadata. - [x] Integration tests with deterministic seed replay. - [x] Basic performance sanity checks (no regression in steady-state runner). - [x] Documentation + example profiles.

How to run locally: python tools/session_synthesizer/burstwave.py --profile benchmark-lab/config/profiles/burstwave-default.yaml --out ./runs/test1 --seed 42  --duration 60
Run the reporter as part of the runner: python tools/reporters/snapshot_reporter.py --run-dir ./runs/test1 --emit-json --compress

Testing: Added unit tests for emission schedules and two integration tests: one that validates deterministic snapshots across seed/commit pairs, and one that asserts the reporter writes per-kernel percentiles without signficant overhead (wall time < +5% on a small CI GPU). CI: new benchci job was added and initially flaked due to an environment mismatch (old CUDA image in the benchci runner). I coordinated with infra to pin a lighter image and rerun. All checks passed on re-run.

Impact: Enables fast local reproduction of temporal spike events and simplifies per-kernel regression detection. Expected to reduce time-to-diagnose for scheduling regressions and guide targeted kernel optimizations.

Notes: This is intentionally conservative — the synthesizer provides profiles rather than stochastic generators for initial stability. Follow-up PRs are planned to add an event-driven stochastic mode and integration with the telemetry-backed corpus sampler.

Related: ENG-2241 (profiling baseline), ENG-2299 (scheduling heuristics experiment).
